references.text: Describes how the fat from a peace offering of small livestock was to be removed and burned on the altar, the same procedure referred to in Lev 4:35
Parallel text about the priest burning the fat on the altar and making atonement for sin so that it is forgiven
Nearly identical wording about removing the fat, burning it on the altar, making atonement, and receiving forgiveness
The same closing formula stating that the priest makes atonement for the sin and it is forgiven
Repeats the formula that the priest makes atonement and the sin is forgiven
Describes the fat to be offered, including the fat covering the entrails, the same type of fat as in the sin offering
The priest makes atonement for the person before the Lord for their uncleanness, using the same atonement language
Hebrews explains that almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness - fulfilling the purpose of the sin offering
Explains that the blood of bulls and goats cannot possibly take away sins, pointing to Christ's perfect sacrifice as the fulfillment of what the sin offering foreshadowed
Forgiveness for sin through confession, fulfilling the sin offering's promise of forgiveness (וְנִסְלַח לוֹ)
